**Accrued into March (USD 16,380 to 2100 Accrued Expenses):**
| JE | Vendor / Invoice | Amount | Why March |
|---|---|---|---|
| JE-00304 | Pinecrest Janitorial PJ-0402 | 780.00 | Cleaning performed 3/28 |
| JE-00305 | Cirrus CDN CC-20260406 | 3,200.00 | Service period = March 2026 |
| JE-00306 | Whitcombe & Ames WA-3402 | 12,400.00 | Legal services rendered March 2026 |

All three have the underlying April invoice **and** the April AP payment register attached as support.

**Excluded:** Lumen Office Leasing LOL-2026-04, $14,500 — this is **April** rent. I verified March rent was already recorded and paid separately (LUM-88858, JE-00221/JE-00238), so accruing it would have double-counted rent.

**Approval:** JE-00306 ($12,400) exceeds the $10,000 senior-accountant authority, so it was routed to you via `request_approval` and sits pending. I deliberately did not split it to stay under the threshold.

**Exception EXC-001:** I could only test the US entity — there is no April invoice or payment-register data in the system for UK or DE. Rather than estimate an accrual without support, I flagged it and left those two checklist items open. That's the one thing worth chasing before sign-off, since auditors will expect completeness testing across all three entities.

One follow-up for April: these three accruals need to be reversed when the April invoices hit AP, or the expense will duplicate.
